title: Multiple savepoints
description: You can set more than one savepoint in the same transaction and roll back to any of them - rolling back to an earlier one undoes everything after it, including any later savepoints. Set savepoint `sp1`, then (by mistake) raise every product's price by 10%. Set savepoint `sp2`, then (also by mistake) delete every row from `order_items`. Roll back all the way to `sp1` (undoing BOTH mistakes). Then correctly apply a 10% DISCOUNT to just the `'Fountain Pen'` product.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: multiple SAVEPOINTs

Six statements in order: SAVEPOINT sp1, the mistaken price increase, SAVEPOINT sp2, the mistaken DELETE, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp1 (discarding both mistakes, sp2 included), then the correct, filtered price update.
After rolling back to sp1, write a fresh UPDATE that multiplies price by 0.9, filtered to WHERE name = 'Fountain Pen'.
expected_behavior: order_items is completely untouched, every product's price is unchanged EXCEPT Fountain Pen, which is now 10% cheaper than before.
solution: SAVEPOINT sp1; UPDATE products SET price = price * 1.1; SAVEPOINT sp2; DELETE FROM order_items; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp1; UPDATE products SET price = price * 0.9 WHERE name = 'Fountain Pen';
explanation: Savepoints nest naturally in the order you create them - rolling back to an earlier one always discards every later one along with whatever they protected, because none of that work exists anymore once you're back before it.

hidden_tests.label: order_items still has all its rows
